Tomato___Late_blight.label: Tomato — Late Blight
Tomato___Late_blight.description: A fast-spreading fungal disease that causes dark, water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems, often fatal to the plant within days in humid weather.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment: Remove and destroy infected leaves immediately. Apply a copper-based or chlorothalonil fungicide every 7-10 days. Avoid overhead watering and improve airflow between plants.

Tomato___Early_blight.label: Tomato — Early Blight
Tomato___Early_blight.description: Fungal disease causing concentric-ring brown spots on older leaves, usually starting from the bottom of the plant.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Prune lower infected leaves, apply mancozeb or copper fungicide, and rotate crops next season to break the fungal cycle in the soil.

Potato___Late_blight.label: Potato — Late Blight
Potato___Late_blight.description: The same pathogen responsible for the historic Irish potato famine — spreads rapidly in cool, wet conditions.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Apply fungicide (metalaxyl or copper oxychloride) at first sign of infection. Destroy infected tubers and avoid planting in the same field for at least 2 seasons.

Corn___Common_rust.label: Corn (Maize) — Common Rust
Corn___Common_rust.description: Reddish-brown pustules appear on both leaf surfaces, reducing photosynthesis and yield if left unchecked.
Corn___Common_rust.treatment: Apply a triazole or strobilurin fungicide if infection appears before tasseling. Choose rust-resistant hybrid seed varieties for future sowing.

Wheat___Yellow_rust.label: Wheat — Yellow (Stripe) Rust
Wheat___Yellow_rust.description: Yellow-orange stripes of spores form along leaf veins; spreads fast in cool, humid climates and can cause major yield loss.
Wheat___Yellow_rust.treatment: Spray propiconazole or tebuconazole-based fungicide at first symptom. Monitor weekly during cool, moist weather and consider resistant varieties next season.

Healthy.label: Healthy Leaf
Healthy.description: No visible signs of disease detected on the scanned leaf.
Healthy.treatment: No treatment needed. Continue regular monitoring, balanced fertilization, and adequate irrigation.
